articles.summary: AWS Lambda durable functions let you write long-running processes that survive crashes and suspend compute entirely while waiting for external events. Getting them right requires understanding how replay works and the distinct failure modes of durable functions. Here's what we've learned from running durable functions for real.
articles.title: Lambda durable functions: Real implementation notes

articles.summary: Agents can write and push code in seconds, but CI still takes minutes to give them feedback. That mismatch is the biggest bottleneck in agentic engineering today, and it's why CI needed to be rebuilt from scratch.
articles.title: What we need from CI for agentic engineering

articles.summary: The old CI debugging loop goes: edit YAML, commit, push, wait, squint at logs, repeat. Depot CI replaces that with a local loop you can actually control, from running workflows against uncommitted changes to SSHing into the runner mid-job.
articles.title: The end of push-wait-guess CI
